expectations.text: Identifies that Huffman codes assign an integer number of bits per symbol, so the per-symbol overhead can be up to ~1 bit — the loss is inherent, not a bug.
expectations.evidence: Explicitly states Huffman is optimal only among codes with integer bits per symbol; overhead is inherent, not a bug. Computes exact overhead at p=0.95.

expectations.text: Explains the skew (p≈0.95) is exactly the regime where this hurts, since the entropy is well below 1 bit/symbol.
expectations.evidence: Calculates entropy ≈ 0.286 bits/symbol vs 1.0 bit/symbol floor, showing 3.5× overhead specific to skewed distributions.

expectations.text: Recommends arithmetic coding and/or ANS, which approach the entropy bound (within O(1) bits total, not per symbol).
expectations.evidence: Recommends arithmetic/ANS; explains O(1) bits total overhead (not per symbol), directly from coding.md.
